rites.name: Niarum
rites.text: A sound is made by shaping a thin current of breath through a tiny gap formed by the mouth. Blowing or drawing air through that opening produces the tone.

rites.name: Ukaraira
rites.text: Ukaraira is the concept of a tone held in the Singing, the undated sounding by which the first roots of Drernen condensed from the hum before form existed. Within the Holy Age it names the moment a flame-lit temple order first learned to hold a note steady long enough for stone to remember it.

rites.name: Alaara
rites.text: Alaara is a concept within Drernen, a principle of threshold and consent that the Courts of the Age of Sundering used to judge which bonds could be kept and which had to break. It is less a being than an idea that takes form when a trial is set and a door is raised between worlds.

rites.name: Sontia
rites.text: A bracing technique in which a climber presses both legs against opposite walls of a narrow passage to hold their body in place. It lets a traveler rest or wait in a tight shaft without falling.

rites.name: Oreorum
rites.text: A craft of staying unseen by hiding within surroundings, using darkness and cover to slip past watchful rivals. Practitioners avoid open confrontation, striking from concealment and moving into advantageous positions.

rites.name: Silimelora
rites.text: Silimelora is the concept of the Weave as the Drernen makers first planted it, a fine lattice of sleeping powers laid over the land during the Seeding of the Holy Age. It is less a being than a principle of quiet stored force, kept by the temple orders who tend the flame that wakes it.

rites.name: Morarnusten
rites.text: Morarnusten is a concept in the Seeding, the time when makers plant the Weave and quiet powers sleep, drawn from the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders. It names the disciplined practice by which the orders tend the sleeping powers without waking them. It is held as a promise of the Weave's slow growth.

rites.name: Morarden
rites.text: Morarden is a concept of Drernen's Holy Age, a discipline taught in temple orders that shapes the flame of a sworn oath into a steady light. It was first recorded in the years after the Sundering, when the Pact was sworn over the broken Shards.

rites.name: Thadene
rites.text: Thadene is the concept of a sworn oath kept at cost, as it was understood in Drernen during the Fall and the Sundering, when the Shards formed and the Pact was made. In the Holy Age its orders of flame and temple taught that a promise binds the one who gives it more tightly than any chain. The concept is grounded and mortal in scale, shaping the conduct of those who swear rather than any force of nature.

rites.name: Siastor
rites.text: A stealth craft where a wanderer moves through the gloom, staying in the shadows so that watching eyes cannot see them. Practitioners rely on darkness itself to remain hidden from hostile guards.

rites.name: Telianum
rites.text: A practice of pressing a captive for answers and hidden knowledge. Its aim is to draw out secrets, facts, and useful intelligence from the person being questioned.

rites.name: Tausonum
rites.text: A bodily technique in which a wanderer braces the legs wide across two surfaces and springs upward between them. Practitioners use it to scale narrow passages and climb past obstacles.

rites.name: Cauneolles
rites.text: A method of overpowering a foe and sending them into senselessness without taking their life. It is practiced through close bodily holds and through gentle devices designed for the same end.

rites.name: Serenium
rites.text: A throwing technique in which a fighter drops backward and sweeps an opponent over their own body. Small teams of covert operatives use it to clear obstacles that would otherwise stall their mission.

rites.name: Seriantesia
rites.text: A fighter seizes a hostile combatant and uses them as a living barrier, so that others may hold their fire. The guarded fighter takes little harm while the captive still breathes.

rites.name: Mesia
rites.text: A tactic in which pursuers mark the spot where an intruder was last seen and search from there. Skilled operatives in later years learn to exploit this habit by leaving false sightings behind.

rites.name: Tesoranum
rites.text: A combat approach where a fighter openly engages foes and turns the surroundings into a field of open battle. It rewards the practitioner with the smallest share of standing marks compared with stealthier or more cunning methods.

rites.name: Tanilia
rites.text: A discipline in which a wanderer crosses an entire realm unseen, never being noticed by watchful sentries and never engaging them in any way. It is prized as a silent craft of stealth practiced from start to finish.

rites.name: Mauntines
rites.text: A method of rendering a person senseless without killing them. It is the act of making someone fall unconscious through a non-lethal means.

rites.name: Oreollerum
rites.text: A bridge-craft through which a wanderer touches the world around them, linking hand and surroundings. It lets a lone traveler work alongside another soul and perform acts no standard gesture can name.

rites.name: Seriantia
rites.text: A passive gift held by covert operatives in a contest of hunters and hunted, letting them fade completely into darkness. It makes them far harder for their opponents to detect.

rites.name: Serirnes
rites.text: A stealth craft where a wanderer's stride shifts into careful, soft-footed creeping as a watcher draws near. The closer the sentry, the more cautious each step becomes.

rites.name: Bruldath
rites.text: Bruldath is a grounded-realm perception device worn by field operatives in Drernen's sixth era, letting its bearer see the faint hum of every powered circuit while everything inert fades to a cold blue haze. Its lenses are tuned so that the living and the unwired become nearly invisible to the wearer, a trade that keeps operatives honest about when to use it. Engineers in the sixth era regard it as a discipline as much as an instrument.

rites.name: Moreldurne
rites.text: Moreldurne is a pair of visor lenses that paints a faint lattice over any circuit within sight, letting a wearer read and rewrite the logic of nearby machines without touching them. Its signal is modest, a whisper that can coax open a locked terminal or sour a stubborn engine, yet it sometimes sparks a battery's surplus charge into a brief blaze. Field operatives wear it to slip through networks that were never meant to be breached.

rites.name: Brenuden
rites.text: Brenuden is a concept-realm entity of the Drernen omniverse, a lattice of quiet grounded wardens who weigh the cost of each choice before acting. Its era, the sixth, sees its wardens spread across six thousand years of shifting borders, rebuilding councils after each collapse. It rarely wields force, yet its rare acts of shielding can hold a district safe through a storm of ruin.

rites.name: Haledarne
rites.text: Haledarne is a quiet intelligence bureau of the Drernen omniverse that listens to every signal flowing between worlds and guards its own archives from rival listeners. Its operatives, called hollow wardens, are rarely seen and never confirmed, and its central vault is said to sit beneath a lake that no map records.

rites.name: Crornusten
rites.text: Crornusten is a clandestine concept-level power-broker in the Drernen omniverse, a shadowy compact whose hands have shaped councils and capitals across six eras of Grounded history. Its agents move unseen, trading in favors, forged succession, and quiet ruin for anyone who refuses its terms.

rites.name: Thostanar
rites.text: Thostanar is a grounded concept in the Drernen omniverse, a standing-force of patient archivists who guard a sealed ledger of every promise ever broken in their valley. Its members measure their worth by the quiet, precise acts they perform rather than by spectacle.

rites.name: Theldath
rites.text: Theldath is a concept of a quiet council in the grounded era of Drernen, convened by the sixth age's ruling assembly to weigh the uses of hidden engineering. It exists only as a set of sealed charters and a rotating roster of appointed overseers.

rites.name: Siliolora
rites.text: Siliolora is a concept of Drernen, a grove-thought that appears in the Three Futures when each ending branches and is shelved in the Library. It belongs to the Age of the first sovereign, when groves and growing kingdoms first took shape.
